nodes.cierpliwie.text.t: You sit for an hour in the chill until the scouts' tongues loosen. You don't hear it all and don't follow it all, but what drifts over is enough: they're after one survivor, and they know he headed for the Ford. The rest drowns in coughing.

nodes.juz.text.t: One raises an eyebrow, the other pretends to sleep. "You again? You were meant to be looking for your own, not for us. We've nothing more for you, and we won't say it twice." They go back to talking, much more quietly this time.

nodes.obozowisko.options.[cierpliwie].te.t: Sit in the shade and listen as long as you can (takes an hour).

nodes.obozowisko.text.t: By the fire, behind a wagon, sit two men in grey cloaks. They talk under their breath, which usually means it's worth listening. Or that you'd rather not know what they do to eavesdroppers.

nodes.podsluch_ok.text.t: "…they're after a survivor from the school, the one from Birchgrove. One lived, the rest are rotting. They know he headed for the Ford." – "And the commander?" – "The commander can't remember what he ate for dinner, never mind who he's seen." They both guffaw.

nodes.podsluch_zle.text.t: One raises his head and looks straight at where you're standing. "Come out, before I haul you out bush and all. Ears are a fine thing, but I'd rather see them on your head."

nodes.rozmowa_ok.text.t: "You ask, so I'll tell you. Not for free, but you look like the sort with nothing to lose anyway." And he talks: about the survivor, about a wanted notice, about someone at the Ford looking the wrong way.

nodes.rozmowa_zle.text.t: "Sit, since you're standing. Talk, since you're silent. No, actually, don't talk, I don't believe you." The scouts go back to their business as if you weren't there at all.
